summary: Deep learning library on PyTorch that gets state-of-the-art results in a few lines, with a free course and book to learn from.

heroCommands.command: Use it in Google Colab with no install

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: fastai is a deep learning library built on PyTorch. It gives practitioners high-level components that reach strong results quickly in vision, text, tabular data and recommendation, and gives researchers low-level parts to mix and match. Its quick start builds an image classifier, segmentation model, sentiment model, recommender or tabular model in about five lines each.
sixtySeconds.problem: Deep learning code is often long and fiddly. fastai's layered API lets beginners get good results fast while still letting experts customize everything.
whoFor: Practitioners who want quick strong baselines
Researchers who want hackable building blocks
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for very concise code, excellent free learning material (course.fast.ai and the book), and a design that's both approachable and deeply configurable.
requirements: PyTorch (install it first for the best version for your machine)

overview: You can use fastai with no installation in Google Colab; every docs page is also a notebook (switch the runtime to GPU). Locally, install PyTorch first, then pip install fastai.
Start with the free course and the book, then the Quick Start and Tutorials in the docs.
On Windows, Jupyter forces num_workers to 0, which slows vision tasks; the README recommends WSL or running from a script. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
